title: Quiz 4 — non-collinear magnets and incommensurate spirals

questions.question: Why can an incommensurate spiral not be simulated exactly with an ordinary supercell?

options.b: an incommensurate q is not a rational fraction of a reciprocal-lattice vector, so no finite supercell is periodic

questions.explanation: Only commensurate q = m/N fit an N-cell supercell; incommensurate q never repeats.

questions.question: What does the rotating-frame method do to every bond matrix?
questions.explanation: Spins of cell R are R_n(2π q·R) times those of cell 0, so the bond coupling seen by the cell-0 frames is J R_n(2π q·R): periodic again.

questions.question: Which condition must the Hamiltonian satisfy for the rotating-frame treatment?

options.b: invariance under rotations about the spiral axis n (Heisenberg, D ∥ n, anisotropy along n)

questions.explanation: Then R_n^T J R_n = J for every bond and the transformed Hamiltonian is translation invariant; SymPhase checks this and refuses otherwise.

questions.question: In the rotating frame, where does neutron scattering see the magnon ω(k)?
questions.explanation: The lab-frame spin correlations mix k with k ± q because the frame rotates with wavevector q.

questions.question: For the J1–J2 chain with J1 < 0 (FM) and J2 > 0 (AFM), a spiral appears when …
questions.explanation: J(q) = 2J1 cos(2πq) + 2J2 cos(4πq) has its minimum away from q = 0 only for J2 > |J1|/4; then cos(2πq) = −J1/(4J2).

questions.question: Hands-on: J1 = −1 meV, J2 = 0.5 meV (examples/vasp/Spiral_J1J2_chain). Spiral wavevector |q| in r.l.u.?
questions.explanation: cos(2πq) = 1/2 → q = 1/6 (period 6a = 18 Å).

questions.question: Hands-on: classical energy gain of that spiral relative to the ferromagnet (meV per site, S = 1)?
questions.explanation: FM: J1 + J2 = −0.5; spiral: J1 cos60° + J2 cos120° = −0.75 → gain 0.25 meV/site.

questions.question: Hands-on: for J1 = −1 meV, J2 = 0.2 meV, what is |q| (r.l.u.)?
questions.explanation: J2 < |J1|/4: the ferromagnet (q = 0) is the ground state.

questions.question: Hands-on: J2 = |J1| = 1 meV (J1 FM). |q| in r.l.u.?
Besides k = 0, where does the rotating-frame magnon ω(k) of a Heisenberg spiral vanish?
questions.explanation: ω(k) ∝ √[(J(k) − J(q))(...)]: J(k) = J(q) at k = ±q (rotations of the spiral plane, Goldstone modes).

questions.question: Hands-on: FM chain with uniform DMI, J = −1 meV, D = 0.2 meV (examples/vasp/Helix_DMI_chain). Helix period in lattice constants?
Same chain with D = 0.4 meV: |q| in r.l.u.?
A uniform DM vector D ∥ chain direction produces …

options.a: a Bloch helix rotating in the plane ⊥ chain
options.b: a cycloid in the plane containing the chain

questions.explanation: The spins rotate about n = D (the chain axis): a helix; D ⊥ chain (interfacial DMI) gives cycloids.

questions.question: What decides the handedness (sign of q) of a DMI spiral?

options.b: the sign (direction) of D relative to the bond

questions.explanation: D·(S_i × S_j) favours one sense of rotation; reversing D reverses q. Without DMI ±q are degenerate.

questions.question: What does SymPhase do when you use --relax in a fixed cell but an incommensurate spiral would be lower in energy?

options.b: it reports the spiral q and energy and suggests --spiral auto

questions.explanation: 'spiral_check' compares the relaxed fixed-cell energy with the optimal single-Q spiral.

questions.question: Hands-on (concept check): for q = 1/6 the spiral is commensurate. What does the explicit 6-site supercell give?

options.b: the same energy per site and the folded rotating-frame spectrum

questions.explanation: Tested in SymPhase: E/site = −0.75 meV in both, and the 6 supercell branches equal ω_rot(k + m·2π/6a).

questions.question: Single-ion anisotropy −K (S·x)² with the spiral axis n = z is …

options.b: not rotation-invariant about z: single-Q fails, SymPhase refuses — use a supercell

questions.explanation: Anisotropy within the spiral plane bunches the spiral (higher harmonics); only anisotropy along n keeps the rotating-frame symmetry.

questions.question: How does SymPhase find the optimal spiral?

options.b: minimising the classical energy over q (grid + Nelder–Mead) and the sublattice phases ψ_i (BFGS)

questions.explanation: E(q, ψ) is evaluated with the rotating-frame bond matrices; the global minimum gives q and the phases.

questions.question: What is the net magnetic moment of an incommensurate planar spiral?

options.b: zero (it averages out over the spiral)

questions.explanation: The moments rotate through all in-plane directions; SymPhase reports net moment 0 for q ≠ 0.

questions.question: Which limitation remains?

options.b: single-Q planar spirals; multi-Q, conical or anisotropy-distorted spirals need a supercell

questions.explanation: The rotating frame handles one q with a rotation-invariant Hamiltonian; everything else uses the general fixed-cell LSWT.
